summary: Tested the new Sanctuary feature (Meditation + Study sub-screens) on Expo web mobile viewport (390x844) and ran a backend smoke regression. Backend: 16/16 pytest in test_sanctus_backend.py (Health, Liturgical, AuthUnauth, AuthenticatedFlow) pass — no regression from the Sanctuary addition (which is frontend-only). Frontend Sanctuary hub renders correctly with both cards (sanctuary-meditation-card, sanctuary-study-card) — deep-link /sanctuary works and tapping the Meditation card navigates to /sanctuary/meditation where breathing-guide, rotating-quote, sanctuary-audio-card, meditation-back, all 4 filter chips (all/piano/harp/chant) and all 5 timer chips (5/10/15/20/30) are present. CRITICAL ISSUE: useKeepAwake() from expo-keep-awake throws an uncaught 'Wake Lock permission request denied' error on Expo Web — this is fired on mount of both meditation.tsx (line 47) and study.tsx (line 43). The dev red-screen overlay then blocks subsequent interactions (timer-pill never showed after meditation-timer-5 click, back navigation didn't return to hub). Needs to be guarded behind Platform.OS !== 'web' or wrapped in try/catch. SECOND ISSUE: tabBarTestID set on the tab bar buttons (tab-sanctuary, tab-today, etc.) does NOT propagate as data-testid on the rendered DOM on Expo Web — none of the 7 tab-* testIDs were found via querySelectorAll('[data-testid]'). This blocks reliable tab-tap automation; recommend using a custom tabBarButton with testID or upgrading to a newer expo-router build that wires testID through. THIRD: tab density — at 390px, the 'Sanctuary' label is truncated to 'Sanct…' on the bar, but the icon + ellipsis are still distinguishable. On a smaller phone (340px) labels may collapse further. INTERMITTENT: Initial Metro bundle hit 'Unable to resolve react-native-web-webview' once (likely a stale start), but the package is present in node_modules and yarn.lock, and after restart the web bundle compiled and the Sanctuary tab loaded. Worth verifying with a clean restart for native builds.

Guard the hook behind Platform.OS !== 'web' or wrap in try/catch. Reference: /app/frontend/app/sanctuary/meditation.tsx:47 and /app/frontend/app/sanctuary/study.tsx:43

tabBarTestID='tab-sanctuary' (and tab-today/-meals/-workouts/-wellness/-community/-profile) does NOT render as a data-testid attribute on the rendered DOM on Expo Web. document.querySelectorAll('[data-testid]') returns 0 tab entries. Tab-tap selectors used by future automation will fail. Recommend a custom tabBarButton component that forwards testID, or move tab tests to native-only. Reference: /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx:36,46,54,64,74,84,100

issues: 7 tabs on 390px viewport — 'Sanctuary' label truncates to 'Sanct…' and 'Wellness' to 'Welln…'. Still readable with icons but on smaller phones (≤340px) tapping precision may suffer. Consider reducing tabBarLabelStyle.fontSize from 11 to 10 or using shorter labels (e.g. 'Calm' / 'Pray') for the new tab.

react_native_issues.issue: Throws 'Wake Lock permission request denied' as an uncaught error on Expo Web when the Wake Lock API is unavailable / denied. Should be guarded behind Platform.OS !== 'web' or replaced with a try/catch wrapper. Reference: /app/frontend/app/sanctuary/meditation.tsx:47 and /app/frontend/app/sanctuary/study.tsx:43

Metro initially failed to resolve react-native-web-webview during the first bundle attempt after the Sanctuary feature was added (seen in /var/log/supervisor/expo.err.log). Recovers after expo restart, but the WebView shim is a known fragile peer dep on web. If similar resolution errors recur, consider lazy-loading SanctuaryAudio's YouTube path (dynamic require) or platform-gating react-native-youtube-iframe behind a Platform.OS check.

critical_code_review_comments: /app/frontend/app/sanctuary/meditation.tsx:47 — useKeepAwake() must be platform-gated; otherwise web users see a dev-mode red-screen and prod users get an unhandled promise rejection.

/app/frontend/src/components/SanctuaryAudio.tsx:85 — useAudioPlayer is called unconditionally even when the track is a YouTube source; on YouTube tracks the player object will be a no-op but the hook still runs. Consider gating the hook inside the Mp3BackedPlayer component (already the case) — but verify with React rules-of-hooks that switching between mp3/youtube tracks doesn't change hook order. Currently the parent renders a different sub-component per kind (YoutubeBackedPlayer vs Mp3BackedPlayer), which is safe.

/app/frontend/src/components/SanctuaryAudio.tsx:103 — the didJustFinish effect calls player.seekTo(0) inside the same effect that flips onPlayPauseChange(false). If the parent's setPlaying(false) re-renders before seekTo completes, this works fine; just noting that seekTo on a player that just finished is racy with autoplay re-entry. Not a blocker.

/app/frontend/app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx — 7 visible tabs on a 390px screen is at the upper limit of usable density. Sanctuary label visibly truncates. Acceptable for MVP, would revisit with a More menu if more tabs land.

/app/frontend/src/utils/sanctuary-tracks.ts:46–95 — Internet Archive MP3 URLs are unverified at test time (no curl-style smoke). If CORS blocks them on web, audio will be silent on the web preview but still work on native — this is called out in the request and acceptable.
/app/frontend/src/components/RotatingQuote.tsx:35 — shuffled(SANCTUARY_QUOTES) runs once on mount via useMemo with []; intentional and correct (avoids re-shuffle on every render).

rca_of_issue: Wake Lock error: useKeepAwake() from expo-keep-awake calls navigator.wakeLock.request('screen') on web. Most browsers reject this without a user-activation gesture immediately after mount, and expo-keep-awake does not catch the rejection — it bubbles up as an uncaught error, which React's dev error boundary surfaces as a red overlay. Fix is straightforward: import {Platform} from 'react-native' and only call useKeepAwake() when Platform.OS !== 'web', or wrap the underlying activate call in try/catch.
